findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker could manipulate the content of the 'secret' file to inject malicious commands.
findings.assumptions: The 'secret' file is attacker-controlled or can be manipulated by an attacker.

findings.title: SQL Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker could inject malicious SQL code into the email body or subject.
findings.assumptions: The email content is processed by a database or an interpreter that executes SQL commands.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: An attacker could send a very large email body, causing a buffer overflow.
findings.assumptions: The email content is stored in a fixed-size buffer without proper bounds checking.

findings.title: Information Exposure
findings.trigger: An attacker could gain access to the 'secret' file and read the password.
findings.assumptions: The 'secret' file has appropriate permissions, but the file system could be compromised.
